---
title: "Notebook UX Contracts"
---

Notebooks are a planned first-class public interface. They must show controls,
artifact-producing stages, diagnostics, results, and cleanup rather than hide
the workflow behind one orchestration cell. No notebook API is implemented in
Phase 1.

## Palace notebook contract

The control surface has seven visible sections:

1. `Design And Geometry Controls`
2. `Meshing Controls`
3. `Solver Controls`
4. `Execution Controls`
5. `Output And Run Identity Controls`
6. `Validation And Failure Controls`
7. `Data Classification And Provenance`

The visible workflow stages are:

```text
Build Component
-> Configure EPR
-> Mesh
-> Config
-> Handoff
-> Physics Results
-> Simulation Performance / Benchmark
```

This contract permits Route A or Route B for the current Surface-EPR direction.
It publishes no private component, selector, dimension, screenshot, config,
mesh, receipt, or artifact.

## AEDT notebook contract

The planned PyAEDT notebook flow retains these fourteen visible phases:

1. Setup and Imports
2. Setup and Run Controls
3. Create Simulation Component / Coupon
4. Initialize AEDT Project / App
5. Import GDS and Build the HFSS/Q3D/Q2D Model
6. Geometry Verification
7. Materials and Boundaries
8. Ports / Nets / Excitations, when applicable
9. Simulation Setup
10. Simulation Configuration
11. Solve and Export
12. Adaptive-Pass Convergence / Solver Diagnostics
13. Results: Plots and Readable Tables
14. Save and Release AEDT

This is a version-locked procedure contract supplied by `scq-ansys-aedt`. It is
planned SCGSim UX, not evidence of a current PyAEDT implementation or live AEDT
session.
